title: Deprecate equality deletes in Iceberg V4
summary: huaxingao restarted the 2024 discussion on deprecating equality deletes, now for V4. She argued they are cheap to write but costly to read, block CDC, row lineage and incremental maintenance of materialized views and secondary indexes, and that alternatives are now practical: the Flink ConvertEqualityDeletes task converts them to deletion vectors using a primary-key index, and the proposed secondary index spec includes a key-lookup index that would let writers emit deletion vectors directly. mxm clarified the Flink index is persisted in Flink state and supported deprecation. manuzhang asked how deprecation would work without an engine-agnostic solution. huaxingao first proposed 'deprecated but permitted', separating it from forbidding writes. stevenzwu and mxm favored forbidding equality delete writes in V4, which would simplify the adaptive metadata tree and give engines an incentive to move. huan233usc asked for benchmarks. huaxingao then changed her proposal to forbidding equality delete writes for V4 tables, with upsert workloads staying on V3 until engines are ready.

positions.stance: Equality deletes should be deprecated in V4 because background conversion and a write-time key-lookup index recover their cheap-write advantage, and they block CDC, row lineage and incremental index maintenance.

Supports deprecating in V4; the ConvertEqualityDeletes index is persisted in Flink RocksDB state, but conversion requires Flink today and no cross-engine way to avoid writing equality deletes exists yet.
Supports deprecation but sees no clear path to do it in V4 before the index work lands, for example for Kafka Connect writers.
Initially proposed 'deprecated but permitted' in V4, with forbidding writes gated on an engine-agnostic path.
Expected V4 to forbid equality delete writes, which would simplify the V4 adaptive metadata tree; the Flink sink would need to produce DVs only in V4.
Soft deprecation gives engines no real incentive to stop; leans toward removing equality deletes for V4 tables while still reading them in V2 and V3.
Conceptually in favor, but asked for benchmarks comparing DVs with single-file commits in V4 against equality deletes in V3.
Changed position to forbidding equality delete writes for V4 tables: it is a format decision that does not require every engine's write-time DV path on day one, since upsert workloads can stay on V3.

outcome.note: The proposer moved from 'deprecated but permitted' to forbidding equality delete writes in V4 tables; the discussion continues in later messages of the same subject and no decision is recorded here.

why_it_matters: The proposal shifted from soft deprecation to a V4 ban on writing equality deletes, which would require Flink and other streaming writers to emit deletion vectors before adopting V4.
